item.title: How to Build a Pipeline Flow Chart in Salesforce Without Revenue Intelligence
item.description:
The Pipeline Flow Chart, Rebuilt in React: A Multi-Framework Field Report

Every new Salesforce release gets the same test from me before I trust it: strip the price tag out of the conversation and ask what the business problem actually is, and whether the fix scales. Multi-Framework’s pitch was React, natively, on the platform. Fine - but React for what, exactly?

A Sankey view showing stage progression between two dates, with the dollar swing attached, isn’t an exotic ask - competitive CRM platforms bundle it into the core pipeline view. On Salesforce, the same chart lives inside Pipeline Inspector’s Flow view and per Salesforce’s documentation, Pipeline Flow chart view sits behind CRM Analytics stacked under Revenue Intelligence. Two licenses, ~$220 a seat per month, most of which buys forecasting AI and predictive risk scoring I wasn’t trying to solve for.

item.title: Vibe Coding, Phantom Dependencies, and Why You Need a Bouncer for npm
item.description:
In the world of enterprise security, Supply Chain Attacks as considered as massive, complex nightmares—think SolarWinds or the XZ Utils backdoor. We assumed they were the domain of nation-states targeting enterprise build servers.

But “Vibe Coding” has democratized the Supply Chain attack.

Today, the default workflow for senior engineering is asking an LLM for a quick fix. The AI hallucinates a solution, and we copy-paste the import statement without a second thought. But LLMs are dream machines, not compilers. They don’t check the npm registry; they predict the next token.

item.title: The Vibe Coding Trap: Architecting ‘Entropy Sentinel’, a Local-First Bodyguard for Your Clipboard
item.description:
The era of “Vibe Coding” has fundamentally changed the physics of shipping software. We aren’t just typing anymore; we are conducting. Between Cursor’s Composer, the Claude CLI, and GitHub Copilot, the friction of writing syntax has evaporated. You describe the feature, the AI handles the implementation, and you stay in the flow state.

But this velocity has a silent tax.

When you are tab-completing entire functions at 100mph, you aren’t auditing line 42 of that generated boilerplate. You are optimizing for “Does it run?”, not " Is it safe?".
